summary: L. Carrington Goodrich (1894–1986) was a Sinologist who studied at Chefoo School and Williams College (~1913–1917). He served as Dean Lung Professor of Chinese at Columbia University (~1945–1961).
Laeticia Söderman is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She earned her M.A. in 2010 from the University of Helsinki, where she was later attested as a graduate student in 2014.

Lajos Ligeti (1902–1987) was an Inner Asian, Sinological, and Tibetological scholar. After studying at Eötvös Loránd University, Eötvös József Collegium, and the University of Paris, he held chairs and teaching posts at Pázmány Péter Catholic University and Eötvös Loránd University.
Lak La Sönam Chö Drub studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Lal Mani Joshi (1935–1984) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Allahabad, Banaras Hindu, and Gorakhpur universities, he held faculty posts at Gorakhpur, Punjabi University, Haverford College, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.
Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi worked in Indology. He served as Jain Pandit at the Central Library of Baroda and held a post at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, attested in 1939.

Lama Jampa Thaye (born 1952) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned a PhD at the University of Manchester. He studied under several traditional teachers and served on the international teaching faculty at Karmapa International Buddhist Institute.

Lama Kunga Rinpoche (born 1935) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ngor Monastery (~1947–1959), where he was Thartse Shabthung in 1959, and founded the Ewam Choden Tibetan Buddhist Center in 1973.

Lama Palden Drolma is a practitioner and scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under traditional teachers including the 16th Karmapa, Jamgon Kongtrul the Third, Bokar Rinpoche, Tai Situ Rinpoche, and Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje.

Lama Thubten Yeshe (1935–1984) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies figure educated at Sera Monastery. He founded Kopan Monastery, Tushita Meditation Centre, and the FPMT, and taught at the University of Virginia and University of California, Santa Cruz.

Lama Tsultrim Allione (born 1947) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned a master's degree at Antioch University, studied under Chögyam Trungpa, the 16th Karmapa, Kalu Rinpoche, and Namkhai Norbu, and founded Tara Mandala in 1993.
Lama Yeshe Gyamtso is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Lama Norlha and Kalu Rinpoche.

Lambert Schmithausen (born 1939) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. After doctoral studies under Erich Frauwallner, he served as associate professor of Indology at the University of Münster and held the Indology chair at the University of Hamburg.

Lance E. Nelson specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at McMaster University in 1986 and held a professorship at the University of San Diego, attested in 1997.

Lance S. Cousins (1942–2015) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology educated at Cambridge. He taught comparative religion at the University of Manchester, taught at Oxford, was a fellow of Wolfson College, and served as President of the Pali Text Society.
Lang Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed a PhD at Yale University (attested 2015), where she studied under Koichi Shinohara, Phyllis Granoff, and Janet Gyatso.
Lang Eun Ra is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who pursued doctoral studies at Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu, Bibhuti S. Yadav, Norbert Max Samuelson, and Leonard Swidler.
Lara Braitstein is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She completed her PhD at McGill University, where she studied under Richard P. Hayes.
Laren Hogen Bays is a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied under traditional teacher Shodo Harada. In 2002, he founded Great Vow Zen Monastery, where he serves as co-abbot.

Larry DeVries is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Minnesota. He held teaching posts at Minnesota, Hawaiʻi, and Washington, a research position at Chicago, and was affiliated with Langara College in 2005.
